questions.prompt: A function inner is defined inside a function outer. Can inner be called from outside outer?
choices: No, the name only exists while outer is running
Only if inner returns a value
questions.explain: The def statement runs when outer runs, and it creates a local name like any other. Once outer finishes, that name is gone.

questions.prompt: Why break a long function into small helper functions?
choices: It makes the program run faster
Each piece can be named, read and reasoned about on its own
Python has a limit on function length
questions.explain: The benefit is for the reader. A helper with a good name replaces a comment with something the code itself says, and a small piece is easier to be sure about than a long one.

questions.prompt: Which of these are true of a nested function?
choices: It can read variables from the function that contains it
It is created afresh each time the outer function runs
It keeps the outer function's namespace tidy
It can be imported from another file
questions.explain: A nested function sees the enclosing scope and is rebuilt on every call. It is invisible outside, which is the point, and that also means nothing else can import it.

questions.prompt: Put these lines in order to make a working nested helper.
questions.explain: The helper has to be defined before the line that calls it, and both defs have to finish before the outer return can hand anything back.
